title: Drift of Low-Cost Temperature Loggers in Vaccine Cold Rooms

headings.text: Drift of Low-Cost Temperature Loggers in Vaccine Cold Rooms

key_sentences: Thirty-six low-cost data loggers were kept in two vaccine cold rooms for eighteen months and compared every quarter with a calibrated reference thermometer.
We recommend a linear drift correction and a recalibration interval of twelve months.
District stores therefore rely on data loggers to show that a cold room stayed within range between two inspections.
Little is known about how this accuracy changes after a year or more in service.
Three models from different suppliers were tested, with twelve loggers of each model.
Model B drifted upwards in every logger, so a cold room that was too warm would have looked colder than it was.
A positive drift is the dangerous direction for a cold room, because it hides a warm excursion rather than raising a false alarm.
Loggers whose drift rate exceeds 0.02 °C per month should be withdrawn from service.
